column1: # Decision 0022 §3: the entry wrapper's descriptor checks with 32-bit pointers,
# run on wasm32 by tests/app/wrapper32.rb. Positive and negative cases, so that
# a narrowed accepted set cannot pass on the refusals alone.
#   kernel  the fixture stem in this directory (its .rb and .contract)
#   args    the C arguments in signature order, comma separated: each buffer's
#           address, each u64 count, then the result pointer. Numbers are
#           decimal or 0x hex; R is the result slot, 8192, in the module's
#   result  the result for ok; `-` otherwise
# No kernel here but at_u8 accesses a buffer element, so an admitted
# descriptor touches no memory: the only store is the result's, and every
# case that is admitted places the result at R or another address inside the
# memory. at_u8's admitted cases read an element inside the memory. A refused case
# must also leave the result slot untouched (decision 0007), which the runner
# checks whenever the slot is inside the memory.
# len_u8_64 and unread_u8_64 declare `# spinel: int64` and have no rows: a
# 32-bit target refuses them (decision 0019, revised 2026-10-21), which the
# runner checks. The u64 count of a 32-bit pointer stays covered here by the
# 32-bit body's rows: read32-over, unread32-top, unread32-high, high-word-*;
# the i64 result's overlap rows went with them, and the i32 result's
